text: This indicates that a causal nexus is required between the offense and the injury. [See HS Services, Inc. v. Nationwide Mut. Ins. Co. (9th Cir. 1997) 109 F3d 642, 647 (applying Calif. law)—“to ‘arise out of’ a termination of employment, the defamatory remark at issue must have been a part of or directly and proximately resulted from the termination” (emphasis added)] [3:300 - 3:309] Reserved. b. [3:310] Exclusions: The standard ISO form CGL policy contains the following exclusions from coverage that may be relevant in employment litigation. (As will be seen, some of these exclusions apply only to “bodily injury liability”; others to “personal injury liability”; and some to both.) The “personal injury” section of a standard-form CGL policy is typically subject to fewer exclusions than the “bodily injury” section. (1) [3:311] “Expected or intended” injury: The policy expressly excludes liability for intentional bodily injury to another: “This insurance does not apply to … ‘bodily injury’ or ‘property damage’ expected or intended from the standpoint of the insured.” [CG 00 01 12 07, Sec. I, Coverage A, ¶ 2.a.
